key_insight: A multimodal temporal-attention model can detect hard-to-see fillet-joint welding defects in real time by combining images and sound, while also explaining which signals drive each prediction.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable in-process quality control for Gas Metal Arc Welding, potentially reducing downstream inspection, rework, and production delays.
method: Trained a deep learning defect detector on synchronized welding images and audio from an industrial collaborative welding robot.
Used a temporal attention module to focus on defect-relevant moments across the weld sequence.
Applied explainable AI to identify important image regions, spectrogram features, and the preferred modality for each defect type.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the attention module improved F1 score to 0.99 on defects including porosity, lack of penetration/fusion, undercut, and cold lap.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the specific robot, sensor setup, and defect distribution, so generalization to other weld geometries or production lines should be validated.
paper_title: Explainable Temporal Attention-based Defect Detection For Fillet Joints in Real-Time Gas Metal Arc Welding Based on Multi-modal Data
